detailed_description: The JSON to C# Converter transforms JSON data structures into idiomatic C# classes with precise type definitions. This tool leverages advanced JSON schema inference algorithms to analyze input payloads, mapping primitive types, arrays, and nested objects to corresponding C# constructs like POCOs (Plain Old CLR Objects) with automatically generated properties, constructors, and JSON serialization attributes. Developers benefit from automated type safety enforcement, eliminating manual translation errors when consuming REST APIs, configuration files, or third-party data feeds. The converter intelligently handles edge cases such as circular references, optional fields (via nullable types), and heterogeneous collections by generating appropriate C# syntax using modern features like record types, init-only setters, and pattern-based type discrimination. Internally, the tool employs a two-pass parsing strategy: first constructing an abstract syntax tree (AST) representation of the JSON, then applying Roslyn-based code generation to emit compile-ready C# code with XML documentation comments derived from JSON keys.
usage_steps: Paste raw JSON data or upload a .json file into the multi-line input editor
Toggle 'CamelCase to PascalCase' conversion for property name normalization
Enable 'Generate XML Docs' to include JSON key descriptions in comments
Click the 'Analyze Schema' button to visualize inferred type hierarchies
Adjust type mappings in the interactive type grid (e.g., force string→DateTime)
Click 'Generate Code' to produce C# classes in the output pane with syntax highlighting
usage_examples: Creating strongly-typed models for deserializing Azure Resource Manager API responses containing nested resource graphs
Generating configuration classes from appsettings.json files with array collections of connection strings
Building telemetry processing pipelines by converting complex IoT sensor data JSON schemas to C# domain models
Rapid prototyping of third-party API clients by transforming Swagger JSON responses into serializable DTOs
